title: Ambient normalized integral strict-model comparison
statement: Let l be prime, E/Q_l finite, and h:U→T any morphism of schemes. Use the thirteen interfaces of [def-weil-pbc-proper-integral-ordinary-data], with the published quotient-normalized coefficient transport and ordinary operations [def-sf-ordinary-integral-pullback-construction, def-sf-ordinary-integral-derived-pullback, lem-tw-integral-comparison-descent, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. There exist a tensor-unit and derived-counit normalized ordinary pullback identification a and a natural isomorphism b from transported completed integral pullback to the derived limit of the actual pulled strict quotient tower. They satisfy PbcProperIntegralModelMatching: all augmentations, both Roos coordinates, and the formula for every K-injective resolution with injective terms are fixed. For every detailed derived object L, transport(eta_L) followed by b_L equals a_L followed by the actual strict-tower completion unit at transport(L). There are no properness, noetherian, dimension, constructibility, completeness, or common-base-field assumptions.

proof.text: Apply the normalized ordinary-pullback identification theorem to obtain a, without completing pullback or comparing either completion unit.
For this a, apply the independently normalized strict-model matching theorem to obtain b and PbcProperIntegralModelMatching.

Form the two natural transformations from transported ordinary pullback to the actual strict completed pullback: transport(ordinaryIntegralCompletionComparison) followed by b, and a.derivedIso followed by the published actual strict-tower unit. Restrict both to good complexes. Their components agree by the good-representative completion-matching theorem. The good-complex localization induces a fully faithful restriction on functor categories (the proved good_whisker_fullyFaithful API), so the two natural transformations are equal. Evaluate this equality at every L and unfold only the published strict-unit component formula to obtain the required equation. Package a, b, model matching and this equation.

lean.statement:
theorem pbc_proper_integral_strict_model_comparison
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] {U T : Scheme.{u}} (h : U ⟶ T) :
    ∃ (a : PbcProperIntegralPullbackIdentification l E h)
      (b : integralDerivedPullback l E h ⋙ integralDetailedTransport U l E ≅
        integralDetailedTransport T l E ⋙ completedReductionTower T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ⋙
          completedTowerPullback h (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ⋙
            completedTowerRlim (pbcIntegralDatum l E) U),
      PbcProperIntegralModelMatching l E h a b ∧
      ∀ L : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E T),
        (integralDetailedTransport U l E).map
            ((ordinaryIntegralCompletionComparison l E h).app L) ≫ b.hom.app L =
          a.derivedIso.hom.app L ≫ completedPullbackComparison h (pbcIntegralDatum l E)
            ((integralDetailedTransport T l E).obj L)

old_proof.text: Identify the completed coefficient maps by their finite projections. Tensor balancing gives the module isomorphism, taking the actual adjunction generators to generators. Localization on flat-term K-flat complexes gives its derived isomorphism with the universal computation-counit equation.

Perform the same balancing at every finite quotient. Naturality of quotient maps produces an isomorphism of whole strict towers. Both quotient augmentations send b tensor x to 1 tensor (x tensor pi_n(b)), so it preserves the augmentations. Restriction along the ring isomorphism preserves products and biproducts, hence transports the Roos shifted cone with both specified coordinates.

Exact countable products make the Roos functor preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Apply the normalized strict Roos comparison to a K-injective tower with injective terms. Its split transition maps make 1-s degreewise split epic; its kernel is the ordinary limit, and the inclusion (limit projections,0) is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the universal derived-limit unit gives the formula for every such resolution. Descend through the resolving-class localization to obtain b and the stated ModelMatching.

The ordinary comparison is represented by (quotient augmentation,0). After an entire-tower resolution its first coordinates are r_n a_n and its second coordinates zero. Functoriality of the resolution gives exactly these coordinates for the actual strict completion unit followed by the limit inclusion. Equality of both coordinates gives equality of chain maps; the computation counits and faithful restriction along good-complex localization give the displayed equation for every derived L.
